parsedVerdict.reasoning:
AdminController sits in the presentation layer. Most of its handlers do presentation work: routing, guards and permission decorators, reading parameters, sanitising input (isNaN on skip/take, parseISO on dateString), turning errors into HTTP responses, and passing calls on to services. Three handlers go further than that.

1. gatherMax and gatherProfileData build queue jobs themselves. Each one fetches the active asset profiles, maps them to job payloads, picks the job name, merges the job options, sets the jobId and chooses a queue priority, then submits the batch. gatherProfileDataForSymbol does the same for one symbol, with its own priority. Choosing priorities and assembling jobs is application-level orchestration. It belongs in DataGatheringService or another application service. The same logic is copied into two handlers, which also suggests it is not presentation work.

2. testMarketData treats a falsy price as a failure and raises an error with a domain message. This is a smaller issue.

Translating a date range into a start date in gatherSymbol counts as input translation, so I did not flag it.
